To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we have developed a system that can find all pages on the web that are relevant to a user query, and (2) the system does this by using a new technique for finding relevant pages that uses the structure of the web, rather than using only the contents of the pages.

1) a page tree is the most appropriate representation for a query; 2) a page tree can be efficiently constructed by a novel page tree construction algorithm; 3) a page tree has a natural ordering, which can be efficiently constructed; 4) a page tree ordering can be efficiently computed; and 5) a page tree with an ordering can be efficiently searched.
the search engine can be used to find a page containing all query keywords and that it can be used to identify the most desirable page tree.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of returning to the user a small number of composed pages that collectively contain the query keywords.
the problem of finding pages that contain the user query keywords in a contextually relevant way.
the following question: given a user query, how to return a set of pages, which collectively contain all keywords, in a manner that is both efficient and easy for the user to navigate?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current search engines are not designed to handle the composed pages problem.
the current Web search engines are not capable of returning the most relevant information to a user query.
the problem of searching the web using composed web pages is still an open problem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are working on a system that would allow users to find pages that contain all the keywords of a query, and to be able to see the context in which the keywords are used.
we have proposed and evaluated a new search paradigm that returns a set of composed pages, where the composition is determined by the query and the user’s preference.
we are interested in finding pages which are related to a given keyword query and are connected via hyperlink and/or frames.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to improve the quality of search results by considering the context of the keywords.
the user’s task of finding a good page tree is made much easier by providing the user with the ability to compose pages from the search engine’s result pages.
the context of the keywords within a page can be exploited to find a small number of pages that collectively contain a large number of query keywords.
